narration.heading: Asteroids
narration.text: You think an asteroid is just a rock? Watch how big they get.

narration.heading: Bennu
narration.text: Bennu is about half a kilometre wide. In 2023, a NASA capsule brought a piece of it back to Earth.

narration.heading: Ten kilometres
narration.text: This one, about ten kilometres wide, slammed into Mexico sixty-six million years ago.

narration.heading: Eros
narration.text: Eros, almost seventeen kilometres long on average. In 2001, a probe made the first ever landing on an asteroid.

narration.heading: Vesta
narration.text: Vesta is over five hundred kilometres wide, and on a dark night you can spot it without a telescope.

narration.heading: Rheasilvia
narration.text: It has a crater five hundred kilometres wide, with a peak more than twice as tall as Everest.

narration.heading: Ceres
narration.text: Ceres, the biggest of all, is about nine hundred and forty kilometres wide. It holds forty percent of the belt's mass.

narration.heading: Our Moon
narration.text: And our Moon, three and a half thousand kilometres across, dwarfs them all.

narration.heading: The twist
narration.text: The twist? The asteroid that ended the dinosaurs was smaller than Eros. Which one would you visit?

skit.text: A ten-kilometre rock ended the dinosaurs? Good thing I'm backed up.

titles: What if you lined up the asteroids by size?
youtube.description: Bennu, the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs, Eros, Vesta and Ceres side by side at true scale, all the way up to our Moon.

sources.claim: Bennu's mean diameter is about 490 m; OSIRIS-REx returned about 121.6 g of it to Utah on 24 September 2023
The Chicxulub impactor was around 10 km across and struck about 66 million years ago, causing the extinction of all non-avian dinosaurs
433 Eros has a mean diameter of 16.84 km; NEAR Shoemaker touched down on 12 February 2001, the first landing on an asteroid
Vesta's mean diameter is about 523 km and it can be faintly visible to the naked eye; its Rheasilvia crater is about 500 km across with a central peak about 22–23 km high
Ceres has a mean radius of about 469.7 km and holds about 40% of the asteroid belt's mass
The Moon's mean radius is 1,737.4 km
